title: What If Humans Disappeared Tomorrow?
lines: What if every human on Earth disappeared tomorrow?
At first, the lights would stay on, | for no one.
Within hours, with no one to run them, | power plants would shut down.
One by one, | the lights would go out.
Beneath New York, pumps keep the subway dry.
Without them, | the tunnels would flood in about {2 days~two days}.
In about {20 years~twenty years}, | broken streets {would/~would} start turning to forest.
Within a few centuries, | steel bridges and towers would rust and fall.
Plastic could outlast them, | perhaps for {1,000 years~a thousand years} or more.
Some bronze statues might keep their {shape/~shape} for millions of years.
But our most lasting {trace/~trace} has already left the {planet./~planet.}
For about a century, | our radio and TV {signals/~signals} have raced outward at light speed.
Today they reach about {100 light-years~a hundred light-years} in every direction, | {they're~and they're} still spreading.
How many stars have our signals already reached? | {About 100~About a hundred}, or {over 10,000~over ten thousand}? | Tell me in the comments.

preroll.line: Our longest-lasting trace has already left Earth.
